# Barndo Beam Co.

> Barndo Beam Co. sells hand-hewn reclaimed wood beams, box beams, fireplace mantels, porch headers and custom beam tables for barndominiums, ranch homes and modern rustic builds. Every piece is Oklahoma Made, made to order and shipped nationwide. Pricing is by free quote.

## Key facts
- Website: https://barndobeamco.com
- Phone: 1-877-870-BEAM (2326)
- Email: barndobeamco@agentmail.to
- Made in: Oklahoma, USA (Oklahoma Made)
- Ships to: the continental United States, by freight or ground carrier.
- How to buy: request a free quote on the website or by phone. You get the price and shipping to your ZIP code within 2 business days, then pay online by card.
- Lead time: made to order. The estimated time is given with each quote.
- Use: decorative. Structural use needs approval from a builder or engineer.

## Products
- Hand-hewn ceiling beams: solid reclaimed beams, 8"x8" or 10"x10", 8 to 20 ft.
- Hand-hewn box beams: three-sided hollow beams that mount over blocking. Lighter than solid beams, 8 to 20 ft.
- Fireplace mantels: 8" face x 10" deep, 6 to 10 ft, natural, medium or dark finish. One-of-a-kind mantel beams and full beam fireplace surrounds are also available.
- Porch and entry headers: 8"x10" or 10"x12", 6 to 12 ft.
- Custom beam tables: dining, coffee and console tables made from hand-hewn reclaimed beams, by free quote.
- Also: corbels, floating shelves, bar tops, stair treads, barn-wood accent walls and reclaimed oak planks.

## Beam Buying Guide

### How do I measure for a ceiling beam or a mantel?
For a ceiling beam, measure the length the beam should cover, and note the ceiling height and which way the joists run. Solid and box beams come in 8, 12, 16, and 20 ft lengths, and other lengths are available by quote. For a mantel, measure the fireplace opening and the overhang you want on each side; stock mantels have an 8 inch face, are 10 inches deep, and run 6 to 10 ft. Send those measurements with the free quote form so we can price the length you need.

### Should I choose a box beam or a solid beam?
Choose a box beam if you want the look of a timber on a finished ceiling and you need something much lighter than solid wood. A box beam is a three-sided hollow beam, open on top, so it slides over a mounting board. A solid beam is 8 by 8 or 10 by 10 inches and it's heavy, so plan for proper support and a carpenter or builder to install it. Both are decorative unless your builder or a structural engineer approves the piece to carry a load.

### How are beams mounted?
Box beams are usually mounted by screwing a wood board, called blocking, into the ceiling joists, then sliding the beam over it and fastening through the sides. Mantels are usually hung on a hidden steel bracket or on lag bolts set into studs or masonry. Solid beams are heavy, so plan the support before they go up. We recommend a carpenter or builder for the install.

### How do I pick a stain to match my floors or cabinets?
Beams, mantels, and tables come in a natural (clear), medium, or dark finish. Hold a sample of your floor or cabinet color next to those three and pick the closest one. Reclaimed wood won't match another finish exactly, and the adze marks and color shifts are part of the wood. If you're between two tones, describe the floors and cabinets on the free quote form and tell us which finish you want.

### How long does a custom order take, and how does a quote work?
Every piece is made to order, so the timing depends on the size and the wood available, and we give you an estimated time with your quote. Use the free quote form, or call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), and tell us the piece, the size, the finish, and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the price and shipping, and you're under no obligation. Once you approve the quote, you can pay securely online by card, and we send photos before your piece ships.

### Do you ship beams, and how are they packed?
Yes, we ship to every state in the continental US by freight or ground carrier, depending on size and weight, and each piece is packed with care. Shipping is quoted to your ZIP code before you pay. Put your ZIP on the free quote form and the shipping price comes back with the wood price.

### How do I clean and care for a hand-hewn beam?
Dust the beam with a soft, dry cloth, and wipe spills promptly so water doesn't sit on the wood. Don't soak the beam or use harsh cleaners, because they can dull a natural, medium, or dark finish. The adze marks, nail holes, and weathered color are part of the wood, so clean the surface and leave the texture as it is. If you have a question about the finish after it arrives, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326) or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to.

### Can I get a table that matches my beams?
Yes, we make dining, coffee, and console tables to order from the same hand-hewn reclaimed beams, in a natural, medium, or dark finish. Tell us the size, the finish, and your room, and mention any mantel or ceiling beams you want it to sit with. No two pieces of reclaimed wood match exactly. We'll send a free quote with shipping to your ZIP code.

## Fireplace mantel sizing guide

How to size a reclaimed wood fireplace mantel: measure the firebox, add overhang, then match a stock length. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#mantel-guide

### How do I size a reclaimed wood fireplace mantel?
Measure the width of the firebox opening in inches, then add 6 to 12 inches of overhang on each side. That total is the mantel length. Stock mantels from Barndo Beam Co. have an 8 inch face, are 10 inches deep, and come in 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 ft lengths, from about $1,050. If the math lands between stock lengths, round up to the next length, or request a custom length. The shortest stock mantel is 6 ft, so a smaller firebox simply gets a little more overhang. Send the firebox width, the length, the finish, and your ZIP code with a free quote for the wood price and shipping.

### How much should a fireplace mantel overhang the firebox?
Add 6 to 12 inches of overhang on each side of the firebox opening. Six inches looks tighter. Twelve inches looks heavier and suits a thick reclaimed beam. A 48 inch firebox plus 12 inches on each side is 72 inches, which is a 6 ft mantel. A 60 inch firebox plus 12 inches on each side is 84 inches, which is a 7 ft mantel. A 36 inch firebox is shorter than the 6 ft stock minimum, so a 6 ft mantel leaves about 18 inches of overhang on each side. Measure the firebox opening, inside edge to inside edge.

### Should I choose a mantel beam or a full fireplace surround?
Choose a mantel beam when you only need the shelf across the top. A stock mantel is 8 inches tall by 10 inches deep, in 6 to 10 ft lengths. Choose a one-of-a-kind mantel beam when you want to approve photos of one exact beam before it is cut. The face is usually 8 to 10 inches, and lengths start at 6 ft. Choose a full beam fireplace surround when you want a mantel plus two legs, three matching beams that frame the opening. Surrounds are available, and custom sizes are quoted. Finishes are natural (clear), medium, or dark. Request a free quote with your ZIP code and we reply within 2 business days with the price and shipping.

### What stock mantel sizes are available?
Stock reclaimed wood mantels have an 8 inch tall face and are 10 inches deep. Lengths are 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 ft, and a 6 ft mantel starts at about $1,050. Lengths longer than 10 ft are available by quote. A full beam fireplace surround, a mantel plus two legs, is available too. Every piece is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide. Finishes are natural (clear), medium, or dark.

## Dining table sizing guide

How to size a custom reclaimed wood dining table: match seats to a length, pick a width and a base, then request a free quote with your ZIP code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#table-guide

### How do I size a custom reclaimed wood dining table?
Count the seats, then match a length. Allow about 24 inches of table length per person. A custom reclaimed wood dining table from Barndo Beam Co. is usually 36 inches (3 ft) or 42 inches (3.5 ft) wide. Four seats fit a 5 or 6 ft table. Six seats fit a 6 or 7 ft table. Eight seats fit an 8 ft table. Ten seats fit a 10 ft table. Twelve seats fit a 12 ft table. Rectangular farmhouse tables run 5 to 12 ft, from about $3,150. Choose a trestle, beam legs, or a beam top on steel, then a natural, medium, or dark finish. Send the seat count, the length, the width, the base, the finish, and your ZIP code with a free quote. Every table is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

### How long should a reclaimed wood dining table be for 4, 6, 8, 10, or 12 people?
Allow about 24 inches of length per person. Four people fit a 5 or 6 ft table. Six people fit a 6 or 7 ft table. Eight people fit an 8 ft table. Ten people fit a 10 ft table. Twelve people fit a 12 ft table. Barndo Beam Co. builds rectangular reclaimed wood dining tables in those lengths, 36 or 42 inches wide, handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

### How wide should a custom dining table be?
A rectangular reclaimed wood dining table is usually 36 inches (3 ft) or 42 inches (3.5 ft) wide. Thirty-six inches seats one person on each side. Forty-two inches leaves room for serving dishes down the center. Leave about 36 inches of walkway behind each chair. Round and square tables from Barndo Beam Co. run 3 to 7 ft across.

### What is the difference between a trestle, beam legs, and a beam top on steel?
A trestle has two end supports joined by a stretcher, so chairs slide in along the sides. Beam legs are thick hand-hewn posts, the same timber face as a mantel. A beam top on steel keeps the reclaimed wood top and uses a black steel base. Barndo Beam Co. builds all three to order. Tell us which base you want when you request a free quote.

### How do I match a dining table to my existing beams or mantel?
Order the table in the same finish as the beams or mantel: natural (clear), medium, or dark. The table is built from the same hand-hewn reclaimed wood. No two pieces match exactly, and the adze marks and color shifts are part of the wood. Name the mantel or beam finish on the free quote form, and we send photos of your table before it ships.

### How do I request a free quote for a custom dining table?
Use the free quote form, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Include the seat count, the length, the width, the base, the finish, and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free, and every table is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

## Coffee and console sizing guide

How to size a custom reclaimed wood coffee or console table: set the coffee table to the sofa, then size the entry or sofa-back console, and request a free quote with your ZIP code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#coffee-console-guide

### How do I size a custom reclaimed wood coffee or console table?
A custom reclaimed wood coffee table is usually about 16 to 18 inches tall, level with the sofa seat or an inch or two lower. Make the length about one-half to two-thirds of the sofa, and leave 12 to 18 inches of walkway on the open sides. Stock coffee tables from Barndo Beam Co. run from 2 x 3 ft to 5 x 8 ft, from about $1,135, with steel legs, in a natural, medium, or dark finish. A beam console table is 32 inches tall, with an 11 by 11 inch solid beam top, in lengths from 4 to 11 ft, from about $1,100. An entry console is often 4 to 6 ft. A sofa-back console sits near the sofa back, about 28 to 32 inches, and runs about the length of the sofa or a few inches shorter. Choose stacked beam legs or a beam top on steel, then send the size, the finish, and your ZIP code with a free quote. Every table is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

### How tall should a reclaimed wood coffee table be next to a sofa?
A reclaimed wood coffee table is usually about 16 to 18 inches tall, level with the sofa seat or an inch or two lower. Measure from the floor to the top of the seat cushion and set the table at that height or slightly under it. Barndo Beam Co. builds coffee tables to order, from 2 x 3 ft to 5 x 8 ft, with steel legs, from about $1,135. Tell us the height on the free quote form. Every table is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

### How long should a coffee table be compared with the sofa, and how much walkway should I leave?
Make the longer side about one-half to two-thirds the length of the sofa, and run that side parallel to the sofa. A 7 ft sofa pairs with a table about 42 to 56 inches long. An 8 ft sofa pairs with a table about 48 to 64 inches long. Leave 12 to 18 inches of walkway between the table and the sofa, and on any side people walk past. Stock coffee tables from Barndo Beam Co. are 2 x 3, 2 x 4, 3 x 4, 3 x 5, 3 x 6, 4 x 6, 4 x 7, and 5 x 8 ft.

### How do I size an entry console or a sofa-back console?
A beam console table is 32 inches tall, with an 11 by 11 inch solid beam top, in stock lengths from 4 to 11 ft, from about $1,100. An entry console is often 4 to 6 ft. A length near 3 ft is a custom size by quote. A sofa-back console sits near the sofa back, commonly about 28 to 32 inches tall, and it should match the sofa or run a few inches shorter so it does not stick past the arms. The stock height is 32 inches. A shelf under the top is available by quote. Request a free quote with your ZIP code.

### Should I choose beam legs or a steel base for a coffee or console table?
Stacked beam legs are thick hand-hewn posts, the same timber face as a mantel. A beam top on steel keeps the reclaimed wood top and uses a black steel base. Stock reclaimed wood coffee tables from Barndo Beam Co. are built with steel legs. A beam console is a solid 11 by 11 inch beam. Tell us which base you want when you request a free quote.

### How do I match a coffee or console table to my beams or mantel?
Order the table in the same finish as the beams or mantel: natural (clear), medium, or dark. The table is built from the same hand-hewn reclaimed wood. No two pieces match exactly, and the adze marks and color shifts are part of the wood. Name the mantel or beam finish on the free quote form, and we send photos of your table before it ships.

### How do I request a free quote for a custom coffee or console table?
Use the free quote form, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Include the table type (coffee, entry console, or sofa-back console), the length, the height, the base, the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free, and every table is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

## Ceiling beam sizing and spacing guide

How to size and space decorative ceiling beams: match the face to the ceiling height and the span, set the on-center spacing, count the beams, then request a free quote with your ZIP code. Full guide: https://barndobeamco.com/#ceiling-beam-guide

### What size ceiling beam should I use for my ceiling height and room width?
Match the face of a decorative ceiling beam to the ceiling height, then to the span. On a ceiling about 8 to 9 feet high, an 8 by 8 inch beam is the stock solid size. On a ceiling about 9 to 12 feet high, 8 by 8 is the usual size. On a ceiling about 12 feet or taller, or across a wide great room, use a 10 by 10. For the span the beam crosses, an 8 by 8 suits a run up to about 16 ft, and a 10 by 10 suits a run of about 18 to 20 ft. Stock solid and box beams from Barndo Beam Co. come in 8, 12, 16, and 20 ft lengths. Space the beams about 3, 4, or 6 feet on center. A face larger than 10 by 10, or another length, is available by quote. These sizes are for a decorative beam. If the beam has to carry a load, have your builder or a structural engineer approve it first. Send the ceiling height, the room size, the beam count, solid or box, the finish, and your ZIP code with a free quote. Every beam is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.

### How far apart should decorative ceiling beams be spaced?
Space decorative ceiling beams about 3, 4, or 6 feet on center. On center means from the center of one beam to the center of the next. About 3 feet on center is a tighter rhythm, and it suits a kitchen. About 4 feet on center is the usual spacing in a living room or great room with 8 by 8 beams. About 6 feet on center is a more open ceiling, and it pairs well with a 10 by 10 so each beam still reads. To space them evenly, divide the width you are spacing across by the number of beams. That result is the on-center spacing, and the center of the first and last beam sits half of that spacing in from each side wall. A room 12 ft across with 3 beams is 4 ft on center. A room 16 ft across with 4 beams is 4 ft on center. A room 20 ft across with 5 beams is 4 ft on center.

### How many ceiling beams do I need for a common room?
Run the beams the long way and space them across the short way. A 12 by 12 ft room takes 3 beams, each 12 ft, at 4 ft on center. A matched package of 3 beams by 12 ft is $5,400, and a single solid 12 ft beam is $1,920. A 12 by 16 ft room takes 3 beams, each 16 ft, spaced across the 12 ft side at 4 ft on center. A matched package of 3 beams by 16 ft is $7,200. A 16 by 20 ft room takes 4 beams, each 20 ft, spaced across the 16 ft side at 4 ft on center. A solid 20 ft beam is $3,200, and a box beam at 20 ft is $3,300. A room 20 ft across takes 5 beams at 4 ft on center. A matched package of 5 beams by 20 ft is $15,000. Packages are matched for color and texture, 8 by 8 standard, at $150 per foot. Send the room size and your ZIP code with a free quote.

### Should I choose a solid hand-hewn beam or a hollow box beam for a ceiling?
Choose a solid hand-hewn beam when you want a full timber, 8 by 8 or 10 by 10 inches. It is solid wood and heavy, so plan the support with a carpenter or builder before it goes up. A solid beam is $1,280 at 8 ft, $1,920 at 12 ft, $2,560 at 16 ft, and $3,200 at 20 ft. Choose a box beam when you want the look of a timber on a finished ceiling and you need something much lighter. A box beam is a three-sided hollow beam, open on top, so it slides over a wood mounting board screwed into the joists, then fastens through the sides. A box beam is $1,320 at 8 ft, $1,980 at 12 ft, $2,640 at 16 ft, and $3,300 at 20 ft. Custom widths are by quote, which helps on a lower ceiling. Both are decorative unless your builder or a structural engineer approves the piece to carry a load.

### Which finish should I choose for ceiling beams?
Ceiling beams come in a natural (clear), medium, or dark finish, the same three finishes as mantels and tables. Natural keeps the weathered color of the reclaimed wood. Medium warms it. Dark deepens the grain and sits well with black window frames and iron. Hold a sample of your floor or cabinet color next to those three and pick the closest one. Reclaimed wood won't match another finish exactly, and the adze marks and color shifts are part of the wood. Name the finish on the free quote form, and we send photos before the beams ship.

### How do I measure for ceiling beams?
Measure the ceiling height from the finished floor to the finished ceiling. Measure the span each beam will cover, wall to wall, in the direction the beams will run. That number is the beam length. Measure the other direction, the width you will space the beams across. Note which way the joists run. Beams usually run across the joists so the mounting board can fasten into them. Note lights, fans, and soffits the beams have to clear. Stock lengths are 8, 12, 16, and 20 ft. If the span falls between those, round up to the next stock length or ask for a custom length. Send the height, the length, the width, the beam count, and your ZIP code with a free quote.

### How do I request a free quote for ceiling beams?
Use the free quote form, call 1-877-870-BEAM (2326), or email barndobeamco@agentmail.to. Include the ceiling height, the beam length, the width you are spacing across, the beam count, the on-center spacing, solid or box, the size (8 by 8 or 10 by 10), the finish (natural, medium, or dark), and your ZIP code. We reply within 2 business days with the wood price and shipping to that ZIP. Quotes are free, and every beam is handcrafted in Oklahoma and shipped nationwide.
